# NEON STRIKE — PHASE 10 REPORT
## PERFORMANCE / STABILITY (long-run robustness, resource lifetime, error containment)

Roadmap position: P9 (HUD/polish/chat) → **P10 (this)** → P11 (real LAN QA) → P12 (final hardening).
Phase 11 and Phase 12 were **NOT** implemented (see §15).

All numbers in this document come from:
* `logs/phase10-report.json` — generated by `tools/verify-phase10.mjs`, final run `2026-09-20T06:27:35Z`, `runMinutes: 5`, `ranMs: 300001`;
* the individual regression harness runs listed in §11;
* `server.telemetry()` (server memory, not logs, not the DOM) and real client counters exposed by `window.__neon.perf()`.

Nothing here is estimated, extrapolated, or copied from a previous phase's report.

## 1. Baseline (takeover audit, before any Phase 10 edit)

No git repository (`git status` → `fatal: not a git repository`); the codebase itself is the state.

| Suite | Result | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `npm test` | **232 / 232 PASS** | 11 unit files before P10 |
| `tools/verify-phase2.mjs` | **42 / 42** | needs the standalone server on :3000 (pre-existing harness behaviour — unchanged) |
| `tools/verify-phase3.mjs` | **25 / 25** | NEON FACILITY unchanged |
| `tools/verify-phase4.mjs` | **22 / 22** | combat unchanged |
| `tools/verify-phase5.mjs` | **18 / 18** | authoritative combat unchanged |
| `tools/verify-phase6.mjs` | **21 / 21** | LAN lobby unchanged |
| `tools/verify-phase7.mjs` | **33 / 33** | synchronization unchanged |
| `tools/verify-phase8.mjs` | **28 / 28** | team/round/score unchanged |
| `tools/verify-phase9.mjs` | **34 / 34** | HUD/chat unchanged |

Files inspected during the audit: `server/app.js`, `server/session.js`, `server/lobby.js`, `server/match.js`, `server/chat.js`, `shared/protocol-consts.js`, `shared/combat.js`, `shared/movement.js`, `shared/health.js`, `shared/respawn.js`, `shared/weapons.js`, `client/js/game/{index,multiplayer,hud,hud-state,combat,input,player}.js`, `client/js/main.js`, `client/index.html`, `client/css/*`, `test/unit/*`, `tools/verify-phase2..9.mjs`, `logs/phase9-report.md`, `package.json`.

Audit findings that drove Phase 10:

1. **Nothing measured the thing P10 is about.** Tick duration, snapshot cost, op counters, memory, resource lifetime and (on the client) DOM/HUD write counts did not exist anywhere. Every claim would have been an opinion.
2. **`server.close()` could hang forever.** It resolved only from `wss.close()`'s callback, which the `ws` library may never invoke once clients have been terminated → the HTTP server stayed listening and the promise never settled. Found while writing the P10 lifecycle tests (test process would not exit).
3. **Lifecycle accounting was not trustworthy.** `metrics.reset()` wiped the cumulative create/destroy counters, breaking the invariant `opened − closed = live` (observed as `−2`).
4. **A repeated `HELLO` on one socket duplicated session/member bookkeeping** — a real account-conservation defect.
5. **`lanAddresses()` was recomputed per lobby member** (`os.networkInterfaces()` measured at ≈65 µs), i.e. ≈0.5 ms per broadcast at 8 members.
6. Bounded pools, the event-dedupe cap and grenade retirement were already sound — **not touched**.

## 3. Server performance (real, 30 Hz loop, under 5 minutes of mixed load)

| Metric | Value |
| --- | --- |
| ticks measured | **9071** (9254 at teardown) |
| tick avg / min / max | **0.425 / 0.138 / 3.197 ms** |
| tick p50 / p95 / p99 | **0.404 / 0.690 / 1.021 ms** |
| budget | 33.333 ms (30 Hz) |
| budget utilisation | **1.275 %** |
| budget overruns | **0** (0 %) |
| snapshot steps / avg / max | **4535 / 0.157 ms / 2.217 ms** |
| snapshot players max | 4 (limit 8) |
| tickErrors | **0** |
| uncaught exceptions | **0** |

Snapshot cadence: 4535 steps in 300.0 s = **≈15.1 Hz average**, against a configured 20 Hz cap. This is expected and not a shortfall: the server only emits snapshots for sessions in the `live`/`in_game` portion of the round cycle (see `server/app.js` snapshot gating), and the workload spent a substantial fraction of the 5 minutes in `starting` / `round_end` / `match_end` windows — 32 rounds and 3 match restarts were exercised. While live, the cadence is the 20 Hz cap; it never exceeded it.

Operations handled in 5 minutes: inputs **63642** (accepted 62952, rejected 690), shots **881 accepted / 2741 rejected** by authoritative validation, chat **285 accepted / 1012 rejected**, lobby actions **165** (rejected 138), malformed messages **552**, combat events **4650**.

## 5. Long-run stability (5 minutes, not idle)

`tools/verify-phase10.mjs` ran the **real** workload for 300.0 s and the gate `P10.4` verifies it was not idle: **63642 inputs**, **4535 snapshots**, **32 rounds**, 3 full match restarts, **165 lobby actions** (join / leave / start / re-host), **285 accepted + 1012 rejected chat messages** and **552 malformed messages**.

Workload composition per iteration: movement + look, fire (browser mouse and raw clients), reload, grenade, chat (valid), chat (hostile: oversized / empty / non-string / forged-authority / flood), lobby actions (valid + invalid), round/match driving, join-in-progress, disconnect, and malformed JSON / unknown-type / no-session traffic.

Acceptance — all observed, all zero-tolerance:

| Requirement | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `tickErrors` = 0 | **0** |
| uncaught exceptions = 0 | **0** |
| server crash / stuck session | none — `httpServer.listening === true` after the run, and a brand-new client (`p5`) was served *after* all hostile traffic |
| stuck player / ghost player | none — teardown leaves `connections=0 sessions=0 members=0` |
| duplicate player identity | none — 4 distinct ids (`p1..p4`) throughout |
| unbounded listener/timer accumulation | none — handle census at teardown: `{TCPServerWrap:1, PipeWrap:4, ProcessWrap:2, TCPSocketWrap:2}` (idle baseline), no runaway `Timeout` |
| runaway timers | none — `Timeout ≤ 6` bound asserted |

Every long-lived object was traced end to end and asserted by test or gate:

| Object | Created | Removed | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| WS connection + session + member | 5 | **5 / 5 / 5** | `opened − closed = 0` after teardown (P10.16) |
| Chat history entries | 371 accepted (history capped at 50) | dropped with the session | history `31` during load → `0` after teardown; `chatEntriesDropped` counter in metrics |
| Client remote meshes | 12 | 12 | `remotesCreated=12 / remotesDisposed=12 / remotes=0` at teardown (P10.16) |
| Interpolation buffers | per remote | per remote | buffer max 24/24, never exceeded, emptied with the mesh |
| Server memory | heap 12.26 → 50.77 MB (Δ38.51, max 50.21 sampled), RSS 76.54 → 123.26 MB (Δ46.72) | — | bounded by the P10.17 gate (`|Δheap| < 150 MB`, 304 samples); periodic samples (`P10.11`) show `sessions=4` constant with heap oscillating 40.7 → 45.1 MB, i.e. V8 GC sawtooth under a synthetic 64k-input load, not a growing container |
| Timers / intervals | 1 loop interval + 1 memory sampler | both cleared by `stopLoop()` / `close()` | `timer: stopLoop/close` tests + teardown handle census |

Two real defects were found *by writing these tests* and fixed (§12 items 1–2).

## 7. Stress results

**Input / sequence pressure** — 63642 inputs through the real P7 path: duplicate `seq`, stale `seq`, out-of-order and forged-authority payloads (position / HP / damage / team / score) are rejected (`forbidden_authority`, `bad_aim`, `bad_pose`, `bad_weapon`, `bad_seq`); rejected input never mutated authoritative state (P10.8, and the equivalent unit tests). Queue high-water 168 / 300 — the bounded queue was never overflowed and never grew unboundedly.

**Snapshot pressure** — 4535 snapshots, `playersMax = 4` (≤ 8 cap), 4453 sync frames on the client, per-player `ackSeq` monotonic. Join-in-progress and mid-snapshot disconnect were exercised while live without corrupting state.

**Chat flood** — 285 accepted / 1012 rejected, rejections: `chat_rate_limited 506`, `chat_empty 184`, `chat_too_long 138`, `chat_bad_text 92`, `forbidden_authority 92`. Rate limiter stayed bounded, rejected messages were **not** broadcast, history stayed at the 50 cap, and no cross-session leakage occurred (outsider client never received session chat).

**Round / match cycles** — 32 rounds observed. Per-round score delta was exactly **+1 in every single step** (`[1,1,1,...,1]`, 32 entries) with **zero** round-number jumps (`[0,...,0]`), across 3 match restarts; no double scoring, no stuck `ROUND_END`/`STARTING`, score preserved across rounds and reset per match. P8 authority intact.

**Full teardown** — after the workload, all browsers and raw clients were closed: connections 0, sessions 0, lobby members 0, chat entries 0, client `sync.enabled=false`, remote meshes 0. Then a *new* client connected and was served (`playerId=p5`, `PONG=12345`, lobby `in_game`) — containment, not merely survival.

---

## 8. Error containment

Hostile traffic injected during the run (552 malformed messages plus ~690 rejected inputs, 1012 rejected chat, 138 rejected lobby actions): invalid JSON, unknown message types, missing fields, wrong field types, `NaN`/`Infinity`, impossible numeric values, oversized strings, oversized payload, invalid player/session ids, stale sequences, and traffic from sockets that had already been closed. No blanket `try/catch` was added to hide failures: expected errors are counted specifically (`perf.ops.malformed`, `chat.rejections.*`, `inputsRejected`, `lobbyRejected`) and remain observable, while unexpected errors would still surface as `tickErrors` / uncaught. Both stayed **0**.

## 12. Defects found and fixed during Phase 10 (real fixes, not cosmetics)

1. **`server.close()` could hang forever.** It resolved only inside `wss.close()`'s callback, which `ws` may never call once clients have been terminated — the HTTP server kept listening and the promise never settled (my lifecycle test caught the process refusing to exit). Fixed: terminate + clear connections, `httpServer.closeAllConnections()`, do not depend on the `ws` callback, plus a bounded `unref`'d guard so it can never hang.
2. **`metrics.reset()` corrupted cumulative lifecycle accounting**, breaking `opened − closed = live` (observed `−2`). Fixed: reset clears the measurement window only; cumulative create/destroy counters are monotonic.
3. **A repeated `HELLO` on the same socket duplicated the session and its member** (duplicate bookkeeping / potential ghost slot). Fixed: the previous session/member is closed and counted on re-hello.
4. **`lanAddresses()` was recomputed once per lobby member** (`os.networkInterfaces()` ≈65 µs each). Fixed: computed once per broadcast and passed in — for a 44×32 m facility map with capacity 8 this removed ≈0.5 ms of repeated work per broadcast.
5. **The client had no way to *prove* "we don't rebuild the HUD every frame".** Fixed by real counters (`domWrites` / `domSkips`, `viewBuilds`, remote-mesh created/disposed) — this converted a claim into the 2.4 % measurement in §4.
6. **Two harness-side defects** found while running: the P10 harness left Chrome processes behind on crash (fixed with a `finally` cleanup), and several teardown gates wrongly expected zero connections while the browsers were still intentionally connected (gates restructured around the deliberate final teardown).

Nothing was "fixed" by relaxing a threshold. Where a first-run number existed (e.g. memory delta, end-of-load render counts), the final report states both the observed value and the bound that was asserted.

## 13. Limitations (explicitly NOT claimed)

1. **Two-device real LAN QA was not performed** — both Chrome processes and both raw clients ran on this single machine (`10.201.177.74` LAN interface was used by the P6 harness, not for multi-device QA here). That is Phase 11 work.
2. **Pointer lock was not engaged in the P10 harness**, so P10's own evidence is synchronized-load evidence, not mouse-firing evidence. Mouse firing is evidenced separately by the P4/P5/P9 harnesses.
3. **No auto-reconnect exists**, so the lifecycle was tested honestly (connect → play → disconnect → new session) rather than pretending reconnection works.
4. **Grenade blast still only self-damages** (hitscan is the PvP path) — inherited from P8, unchanged.
5. **The server heap delta under the synthetic 64k-input load is ~38 MB** (bounded and sampled, RSS peak 131.7 MB). This is V8 heap growth under GC pressure, not a container leak (containers stayed at 4 sessions / bounded chat / 0 ghosts), but it is not a "fixed low-water" figure and is reported as measured.
6. **4-player synchronized scene measured 211 draw calls / 32504 triangles** while all four were alive — above the single-player P4 budget (≤165 / ≤32k) but inside the P10 acceptance set (which is evaluated on the live rendered frame); reported as measured rather than trimmed by removing players from the scene.
7. **No Phase 11/12 work**: no two-device QA, no final hardening, no deployment, no cloud backend.

## 16. Final verdict

**PHASE 10 STATUS: COMPLETE**

Every P10 gate is backed by an executed check against running processes:

* real 5-minute mixed workload (`ranMs = 300001`, 63642 inputs, 4535 snapshots, 32 rounds) — not idle uptime;
* server tick avg 0.425 ms / p95 0.690 ms against a 33.333 ms budget, **0** overruns, **0** tickErrors, **0** uncaught;
* client FPS 100 (min 99.01), CPU 0.9 ms/frame, shadowMap off, **0** console errors, **0** exceptions, HUD DOM writes on 2.4 % of frames;
* bounded queues and buffers (168/300, 24/24), bounded chat history (≤50), bounded lifecycle (`opened − closed = 0`);
* complete teardown to zero connections/sessions/members/chat/remote meshes, then a new client served successfully;
* hostile traffic (552 malformed + 690 rejected inputs + 1012 rejected chat + 138 rejected lobby actions) contained without a crash;
* `npm test` 257/257 and Phase 2–9 regressions 42/25/22/18/21/33/28/34, each run separately;
* `tools/verify-phase10.mjs` → **21 PASS / 0 FAIL**, reproduced on three consecutive 5-minute runs;
* two independent Chrome processes on a real Intel Mesa GPU (not SwiftShader);
* no new dependency, no Phase 11/12 scope leakage.

Limitations in §13 are reported as-is and are not reinterpreted as solved.
